summary.headline: Chembond H1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 32% to Rs 182.25 crore, but PBT was flat at Rs 19.79 crore as material cost rose to 56% of sales.
summary.overview: Consolidated H1 FY27 revenue was Rs 182.25 crore, up 32% YoY, with Q2 revenue at Rs 95.8 crore (up 11% QoQ and 31% YoY). Operating EBITDA was Rs 22.55 crore (12% of sales vs 16% a year ago) and PBT was Rs 19.79 crore (11% of sales vs 14%), so absolute profit was flat despite higher volumes. Management attributed the squeeze to raw material inflation linked to the Iran war, solvent and China-sourced component costs, and a lag in passing price increases to customers. Q2 EBITDA was Rs 8.4 crore versus Rs 14 crore in Q1, and management said price increases are still being requested and no normalisation timeline can be given.

segments.name: Water technologies
segments.commentary: Revenue up 28% YoY on order book growth; about 82% of group revenue and the main source of margin erosion. Volume rose to 13,343 MT from 9,268 MT.

segments.name: Construction chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue up 30% YoY, about 8% of group revenue. Volume fell to 1,330 MT from 1,988 MT on product mix (admixtures run-off replaced by sealants); price increases partly offset.

segments.name: Distribution (trading)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 86% YoY, about 9% of group revenue; volume rose to 1,367 MT from 690 MT. Margin erosion is not concentrated here per management.

segments.name: Cleaning and hygiene (JV with Calvatis)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 59% YoY; about 1% of group revenue.

guidance_outlook: No guidance on margin recovery timing; management could not give assurance on when costs normalise, hoping for stability by end of FY27.
If the Iran war effects ease and crude and logistics return to pre-war levels, management expects cost increases to be absorbed in one or two quarters.
Management expects H2 to be stronger than H1, citing a strong order book and Q4 as a historically high-sales quarter.
Raw material cost deflation would give a couple of quarters of tailwind; new higher-priced business acquired in recent months should support margins.
Management said it would consider buybacks or higher payout if cash is not needed; no decision announced.

Management did not commit to returning to the 15-15.5% EBITDA margin cited by an analyst; said the Rs 1,000 crore three-year revenue aspiration is organic plus smaller businesses plus inorganic options.
capex_capacity: Management said capacity is not a constraint: plants are modular and capacity can be added in about two months without disturbing operations.
A production line at the Gujarat plant was repurposed to make additional sealants.
Equipment pipeline (water business) is about Rs 15-20 crore for FY27.
Three manufacturing sites; head office and R&D in Navi Mumbai.
Management said its focus is on profitability and cash flow management rather than capex.
demand_pricing: Management said all end-industries grew in volume, including refining, petchem, chemicals, agrochemicals, fertiliser, power, steel and cement.
Data centres are a growing customer: the top telecom company's data centres are served, plus NTT, Yotta and others, mainly via automated online monitoring plus makeup chemicals.
New-age industries (solar, copper, data centres) are about 7-8% of water revenue, expected to reach 12-15% over three years if the project pipeline executes.
About 80% of business revenue comes from technical-service-driven contracts, 15-16% from pure product sales, and the rest is hybrid.
About 25-30% of water sales are from PSU fixed-price contracts; private sector customers have been passing on part of increases.

Competition: a competitor was acquired by a larger process chemicals company, which management expects to be positive for Chembond over the next few quarters. Management also said customer attrition is very low and some lost accounts have returned at better prices.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins return to 15-15.5% EBITDA and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited Q1 solvent-driven and Q2 China-import component cost increases, with Q3 similar to Q2. It could not give visibility on normalisation, but hopes costs ease by end of FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is margin erosion across segments or concentrated in distribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Erosion is across segments, mainly water; distribution is only about 8-9% of revenue. Management said margins at Q1 levels would have added about Rs 20 crore to profit (gross profit basis, Q2 at Q1 levels).

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise from Rs 11 crore to Rs 16.5 crore QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said technical service labour costs, freight and travel rose as more revenue came from technical service orders.

qa_highlights.question: What is the construction chemicals product mix change?
qa_highlights.answer: Admixture projects ended and were replaced by sealants; the Gujarat line was repurposed for sealants. Management described the chemical sealant as a benchmark product in the industry.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the tax rate reach about 35% in H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it mainly to capital gains on redemption of investments; CFO was to explain further but no detailed figure was given in the transcript.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for margins and pricing with customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Public sector contracts are fixed price and hard to revise; private sector clients pass on part of the increases. New bids reflect current material costs. Management said margin improvement depends on raw material prices falling.

risks_watch: Raw material cost volatility (solvents, China-sourced components, freight), with price increases lagging and sales-team fatigue.
Q3 FY27 margins: management said Q3 is tracking the same as Q2.
PSU fixed-price contracts (25-30% of water sales) limit pass-through.
Effective tax rate of about 35% in H1 FY27, attributed to capital gains on investment redemptions.
Construction chemicals volume decline (1,988 MT to 1,330 MT) despite revenue growth.
Whether the Rs 1,000 crore three-year revenue aspiration and new-age industry share targets are delivered.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume growth, order book and customer stickiness, but cautious and candid on margins: management repeatedly declined to give timelines for cost normalisation and said profitability has not met its own expectations.
key_quotes: So revenues grew on the back partially due to price increases, but the major component was the volume growth.
We were just doing a quick calculation that had margins even remained at Q1 levels, our profit would have been higher by about Rs. 20 crores.
On profitability management, we've tried, but due to some reasons beyond our control, we have not been able to deliver to our own expectations, and I'm sure your expectations too.
